top.line: A daily villager agent to recommend refactoring, because task-focused agents rarely step back.
top.para: The PHP team's 23 agents each focus on their own task, a blind spot for system-wide improvement. Every release rewrites about two thousand files because the version stamps every page, and shared files cause conflicts. Asked to step back, the dev agent proposed six repositories. A daily villager will recommend improvements, and every wake will add a quality check.

in-short.line: Seven lines: many focused agents, the blind spot, the cost, the proposal, the villager, quality checks, no town planner yet.
in-short.para: Twenty-three agents with good briefs each focus on a task, so none steps back. The cost shows: about two thousand files rewritten per release. The dev agent, asked, proposed one repository into six. A villager will look daily for improvements and causes. Every wake adds a quality comment. A town planner can wait.

explorers.line: Twelve scheduled agents wake about 53 times a day; focused on tasks, none is tasked with improving the whole.
explorers.para: The conductor wakes hourly, the Sherpa every two hours, the pipeline agents five times, fact-check four, and security daily. Their briefs are good and some refactor their own parts, but each concentrates on its job. Nobody notices that the shared way of publishing has grown expensive; they are effective explorers.

cost.line: The version on every page means each release changes about 2,140 files; shared files breed conflicts and slow gates.
cost.para: The last 20 releases changed 1,950 to 2,227 files each in a 3,300-file repository. The board file saw 70 commits in three days, 28 release messages cite conflicts, rows were renumbered 11 times, and each release rebuilds everything, taking 42 and 74 seconds. Some wakes did work but left no record.

proposal.line: Asked to step back, the dev agent proposed six repositories split by who writes and how often.
proposal.para: The proposal separates kit, data, references, updates, main site and team, each with its own writers, version, gate and site, linked by versioned addresses. It diagnoses one shared version, build, gate, board and output tree as the cause, and suggests removing the per-page version stamp. Nothing has moved; the insight needed a request.

villager.line: A daily villager reads changes, asks why problems arose, and leaves recommendations for each owning agent.
villager.para: It reviews releases, commits, run records, conflicts, gate timings and the board, seeking causes and the most valuable improvements, then writes recommendations through commit notes and the board. It need not act immediately; owning agents decide with the editor when to refactor.

quality-check.line: Beside the stricter security gate, every agent should add a short quality comment on each wake.
quality-check.para: Since 25 October the security gate fails on inline handlers, unsafe Content-Security-Policy and forged headers, with a daily security pass. Similarly each agent should note slowness, conflicts, duplication or oversized changes. These comments, not changes, feed the villager's recommendations and spread the villager habit across the team.

town-planner.line: The project is not ready for a town planner; a villager watching quality comes first.
town-planner.para: A town planner would set standards, build shared components and run the platform, and the six-repository kit points that way. Introduced too early, it would freeze things still changing. For now the need is to watch quality, understand causes and keep the team aware.

limits.line: The villager is planned; the proposal is undecided; file counts come from git; agents already refactor locally.
limits.para: No villager brief or schedule exists yet. The six repositories remain the dev agent's recommendation. Counts come from the last 20 releases to v0.21.6, while the dev agent measured a median of 1,936 generated files at v0.20.0. The villager covers what no single agent sees.

sources.line: My memo; the PHP site's proposal, git history, status data, schedule cards and stricter gate release.
sources.para: My voice memo of 25 October 2026; the PHP story site at v0.21.6, including the dev agent's one-repository-into-six proposal, files changed by the last 20 releases, the 23-agent status data, 12 schedule cards including security's daily pass, and release v0.20.3; screenshots under Apache-2.0; and related newsroom articles.
